Devicon — usage rules
=====================

Source: https://github.com/devicons/devicon
License: MIT (Copyright (c) 2015 konpa)
Per-tool trademarks: each Devicon icon depicts a third-party brand whose
                     trademark policy applies SEPARATELY to USE. The Devicon
                     MIT grant covers redistribution of the icon files only.

Use Devicon icons to IDENTIFY the depicted tool, language, framework, or
platform — alongside Azure / Fabric / Kubernetes / FluentUI icons in
architecture diagrams, DevOps pipeline diagrams, tech-stack legends, and
similar use cases.

What you MUST NOT do:
  - Don't use a Devicon icon to represent YOUR product or service. The icon
    of a third-party tool is a brand identifier for THAT tool, not for
    anything you build on top of it. Using the Python icon to label a service
    you wrote in Python is fine ("backend (Python)"); using the Python icon
    AS YOUR PRODUCT LOGO is not.
  - Don't recolor, crop, flip, rotate, or otherwise modify the icon shape —
    each depicted brand's trademark policy is likely to require unmodified
    presentation, and recoloring may infringe the trademark even if the MIT
    license technically permits derivative works.
  - Don't claim affiliation with, sponsorship by, or endorsement from the
    depicted brand owner solely on the basis of using their icon in a diagram.

What you SHOULD do:
  - Pair the icon with the brand's word mark as a label (e.g. icon next to
    "Python", "Docker", "PostgreSQL") — same convention Microsoft mandates
    for Azure / Fabric icons, and a per-brand trademark courtesy.
  - Consult the depicted brand's trademark policy if you have any use case
    beyond plain identification in an architecture diagram (e.g. marketing
    materials, commercial products, conference signage).
  - For commercial-grade clarity, link to https://github.com/devicons/devicon
    in your project README so reviewers can verify the redistribution chain.

This project is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by Devicon,
konpa, or any of the brands depicted in the icons. The icons are redistributed
in unmodified form for use in software architecture diagrams under the MIT
license grant.

This file is the per-vendor USAGE-RULES counterpart to dist/Azure/USAGE-RULES.txt
and dist/Fabric/USAGE-RULES.txt.

For full license text and per-source attribution, see NOTICE at the repository
root.
